subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value:
AN EMPTY-BODIED `if` IS ELIDED WHOLE BY THE MWCC FRONT END -- COMPARISON, OPERAND LOADS AND ALL -- SO IT IS NEVER THE LEVER FOR REPRODUCING A TARGET'S DEAD COMPARE. The only thing that survives an emptied body is a VOLATILE-qualified operand read, which survives as a side effect and not as part of the comparison.

WHY THIS NEEDS SAYING. A target that shows a compare with no consumer -- `cmpw`/`cmpwi` whose cr0 is overwritten before any branch reads it, with no branch and no body anywhere near it -- is a common and very legible residual, and the intuitive cure is to write the guard with an empty body so that 'only the compare is left'. That reasoning is backwards about WHICH COMPILER PASS removes what. MWCC's front end discards a conditional statement whose body is syntactically empty before any instruction is emitted for it, so the comparison never reaches the instruction stream at all. The target's dead compare comes from the opposite history: the comparison WAS emitted for a non-empty body, and a LATER pass removed the body and then the branch, leaving the already-scheduled compare stranded. Front-end elision and late dead-code elimination are not interchangeable, and only the second produces a dead compare.

THE TWO MEASUREMENTS, and note that they fail in opposite directions, which is what makes the rule rather than one anomaly. On LinkItemTriggers the guard's operands are two `*(volatile s8*)` reads: emptying the body left the instruction count untouched at 158 because the two `lbz` are volatile side effects, but the `extsb`/`extsb`/`cmpw` the target wants still did not appear -- so an empty body does not preserve a compare even when its operands are preserved. Dropping the volatile as well took the count to 156, confirming the loads were surviving only as side effects. On AddLocatorInstList the guard's operand is a plain SDA global: emptying the body took 421 -> 416, removing the surplus `bge`+`li` AND the `lwz`+`cmpwi` that the target keeps -- so with no volatile anywhere, the elision reaches the loads too.

OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE. When a residual is 'target has a dead compare we lack', screen this law FIRST and do not spend the empty-body probe; it is a measured null in the best case and a count regression in the ordinary one. Reach instead for a body that is NON-EMPTY in source and dead only after optimization. One reconstruction hypothesis of that shape was also measured and REFUTED on AddLocatorInstList: making the guarded store redundant is not sufficient -- `selected = 0; if (selected > sLastPlayerStart) { selected = 0; }` keeps both the branch and the redundant `li`, and moving the initialization to the declaration (`s32 selected = 0;`) did not remove them either while regressing `real` 306 -> 452 through a whole-function colouring cascade. So the source shape that leaves a stranded compare is still unidentified, and both the empty-body axis and the redundant-conditional-store axis are now closed by measurement.

COROLLARY FOR THE VOLATILE SCAFFOLD. Where a scaffold of volatile-qualified operand reads is already in the tree to reproduce target-only loads, this law says the scaffold is doing its job and the missing compare is a SEPARATE problem: do not remove the scaffold while chasing the compare. On LinkItemTriggers the scaffold is independently proven correct by the target's instruction stream -- the dead compare sign-extends BOTH operands, whereas the immediately preceding live compare on the same field needs only one `extsb` because MWCC had the value already extended, so the target genuinely re-reads both operands and the volatile is what reproduces that.
